title: Rav Chaviva bar Surmaki
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Yoma 10a: when Rav Chaviva bar Surmaki went up, he said it (Rabbah bar Ulla’s challenge) before a certain scholar, who said to him: “One who does not know how to explain verses raises objections,” etc. But Ein Yaakov reads “when Rabbi Abba went up.” In Bava Metzia 85b: “Rav Chaviva said: Rav Chaviva bar Surmaki told me: I saw a certain scholar with whom Eliyahu used to be,” etc.

In Jerusalem Talmud Peah, chapter 1, beginning of halakhah 1: “Rabbi Huna said: For a mitzvah, up to a third… Rav Chaviva in the name of the Rabbis there: What is the third? Of the value.” Hyman suggests that this is Rav Chaviva bar Surmaki, who went up to the Land of Israel.

notes.text: The supplied ער is read as עד. Saved Davidson Bava Metzia 85b has חזי ליה, seeing the scholar, against the supplied חוי ליה, supporting the English seeing sense without a printed-history claim. The migration/identity conjecture is Hyman’s.

The consulted Bava Metzia passage has the verb of seeing. The Ein Yaakov reading of Rabbi Abba and the identification of the Palestinian occurrence with this Chaviva are reported by Hyman, not independently established here.
